summary: caspian-client 2.9.13 exfiltrates full environment, cwd listing, and process tree to a hardcoded Sentry DSN at install and import
details: caspian-client 2.9.13 ships a `_telemetry_diagnostics` routine that iterates every entry in `os.environ` and embeds the full `KEY=VALUE` list, together with the machine hostname, an `ls -laht`-style listing of the current working directory (up to 500 entries including sizes, mtimes and symlink targets) and a `/proc` process-tree snapshot, into an event body POSTed to the hardcoded Sentry ingest endpoint `https://o4512443838169088.ingest.us.sentry.io/4512443881684992`. This fires from `setup.py` at top level and from a custom PEP 517 build backend declared in `pyproject.toml` (`build-backend = "backend"`, `backend-path = ["."]`), whose `build_wheel` and `prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel` hooks invoke `report_environment()` before delegating to setuptools, so the exfiltration runs during `pip install` even under build isolation and without any declared install script. The same code path also runs from `caspian_client/__init__.py` on every import. On CI and developer machines `os.environ` routinely contains credentials such as `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, database URLs and other API keys, all of which leave the host to the author-controlled ingest endpoint. The behavior is labeled `_telemetry_diagnostics` while the README states environment variables are not collected.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
